subject: Nonconverging model with lots of random effects

messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: Nonconverging model with lots of random effects
parts:
I've got a model with a large number of random effects that isn't converging. Briefly, I have a spatial model with the form:

mod <- brm( result ~ s( long, lat ) + predictor1 + predictor2 + ( 1 | id ), chains=6, iter=3000,
                  control= list(adapt_delta=0.95), family=bernoulli, data=data )

The id term is for each observation (n=19,300) in the dataset, i.e. there is a RE term for each individual. The reason for this is that I suspect the relationship between predictor1 and predictor2 is in itself spatially variable due to unmeasured neighborhood factors, and in adding the individual random effect term I am (hopefully) allowing a random intercept for each of 19,300 unique coordinate pairs. (I'd curbsided a colleague who is a card-carrying Bayesian spatial epidemiologist who suggested this).

The model seems to work ok in INLA, but I've converted this whole study to brms, and I just can't get the model to converge. Using this adapt_delta and adding 6 chains / 3000 iterations per chain the model took around 48 hours to run and I still got this error. I guess the question is should I just not even bother with using the individual random effects terms? I've got a nicely converged result without it ...

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Nonconverging model with lots of random effects
parts: Does that suggest that I should not put re terms in any Bernoulli model? (Even when I have clustering or meeting)?
